entries.sanskrit: चतुर्दशे निदानं तु तद्-वधे वक्तुम् उच्यते । सन्ध्यायां कश्यपाद् गर्भ-सम्भवः कामतो दितेः ॥
entries.literal_english: In the fourteenth chapter the cause of his killing is described: Diti conceived from Kaśyapa because of desire at twilight.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: caturdaśe nidānaṃ tu tad-vadhe vaktum ucyate | sandhyāyāṃ kaśyapād garbha-sambhavaḥ kāmato diteḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: तेनैव येन भूमिर् उद्धृता । अनुशुश्रुम त्वन्-मुखात् ॥२॥
word_for_word: by whom the earth was lifted
entries.literal_english: By that same Hari by whom the earth was lifted. We heard this from your mouth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.

entries.sanskrit: मृधो युद्धम् ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: Mṛdha means battle.

entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: साधुत्वे हेतुः, यद् यस्मात् त्वं हरेर् अवतार-कथां पृच्छसीति । मृत्योः पाशं विशातयति मोचयतीति तथा ॥५॥
entries.literal_english: The reason he is called “saintly” is that you have asked about Hari’s incarnation-story, which loosens and releases the noose of death.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sādhutve hetuḥ, yad yasmāt tvaṃ harer avatāra-kathāṃ pṛcchasīti | mṛtyoḥ pāśaṃ viśātayati mocayatīti tathā ||5||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एव दर्शयति । यया कथया उत्तानपदः पुत्रो ध्रुवः । मुनिना नारदेन । अर्भक एव । यदा ध्रुवाय सुनन्दादिभिर् विमानम् आनीतं तदास्य देह-त्यागोऽपेक्षितः स्याद् इति मत्वा मृत्याव् आसन्नेऽपि देहं न तत्याज, किन्तु सोपान इव तस्य मूर्ध्नि पदं दत्त्वा विमानम् आरुह्य विष्णु-पदम् आरूढः । वक्ष्यति हि--- > परीत्याभ्यर्च्य धिष्ण्याग्र्यं कृत-स्वस्त्य् अयनो द्विजैः । > > इयेष तद् अधिष्ठातुं बिभ्रद् रूपं हिरण्मयम् ॥ \[भा।पु। > ४.१२.२९\]इति ॥६॥
word_for_word: the celestial vehicle was brought by Sunanda and others
he did not abandon the body
sopāna iva tasya mūrdhni padaṃ dattvā
placing his foot on his head as on a step
entries.literal_english: He now illustrates this. By the story in which Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, was instructed by the sage Nārada while still a child, Dhruva ascended to Viṣṇu’s abode. Even when the celestial vehicle was brought for him and bodily death was near, he did not abandon his body; he placed his foot on Death’s head as on a step and boarded the vehicle.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tad eva darśayati | yayā kathayā uttānapadaḥ putro dhruvaḥ | muninā nāradena | arbhaka eva | yadā dhruvāya sunandādibhir vimānam ānītaṃ tadāsya deha-tyāgo’pekṣitaḥ syād iti matvā mṛtyāv āsanne’pi dehaṃ na tatyāja, kintu sopāna iva tasya mūrdhni padaṃ dattvā vimānam āruhya viṣṇu-padam ārūḍhaḥ | vakṣyati hi--- > parītyābhyarcya dhiṣṇyāgryaṃ kṛta-svasty ayano dvijaiḥ | > > iyeṣa tad adhiṣṭhātuṃ bibhrad rūpaṃ hiraṇmayam || \[bhā|pu| > 4.12.29\]iti ||6||

entries.sanskrit: तयोः सङ्ग्रामे हेतुं वक्तुम् इतिहासं प्रस्तौति---अथेति । अनुपृच्छतां देवानां ब्रह्मणा वर्णित इतिहासो मया श्रुतः ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: To explain the cause of their battle, he begins the history: “Then.” I heard from Brahmā the history he had related in answer to the gods’ questions.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tayoḥ saṅgrāme hetuṃ vaktum itihāsaṃ prastauti---atheti | anupṛcchatāṃ devānāṃ brahmaṇā varṇita itihāso mayā śrutaḥ ||7||

entries.sanskrit: देव-प्रश्न-प्रस्तावाय प्रथमं हिरण्याक्ष-हिरण्यकशिपूत्पत्ति-प्रसङ्गम् आह---दितिर् इत्य्-आदिना यावद् अध्याय-परिसमाप्तिः । मरीचेः पुत्रं कश्यपम् । हृच्-छयः कामः, तेन अर्दिता । अतः सन्ध्यायाम् एव कामितवती ॥८॥ तद् अप्य् \[अग्न्य्-अगारे\] अग्निहोत्र-शालायम् । तत्रापि समाहितम् । अग्निर् जिह्वा यस्य । यजुषां यज्ञानां पतिं पुरुषं श्री-विष्णुम् ॥९॥
word_for_word: the account of the birth of Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu
that too, in the fire-sacrifice hall
the Lord of sacrifices, the Supreme Person
entries.literal_english: He first introduces the birth of Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu, continuing to the end of the chapter. Kaśyapa was the son of Marīci. Diti was afflicted by the impulse of desire and therefore desired him at twilight. The place was the fire-sacrifice hall, where the concentrated Lord, whose tongue is fire, the Lord of sacrifices, Śrī Viṣṇu, was being worshiped.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: deva-praśna-prastāvāya prathamaṃ hiraṇyākṣa-hiraṇyakaśipūtpatti-prasaṅgam āha---ditir ity-ādinā yāvad adhyāya-parisamāptiḥ | marīceḥ putraṃ kaśyapam | hṛc-chayaḥ kāmaḥ, tena arditā | ataḥ sandhyāyām eva kāmitavatī ||8|| tad apy \[agny-agāre\] agnihotra-śālāyam | tatrāpi samāhitam | agnir jihvā yasya | yajuṣāṃ yajñānāṃ patiṃ puruṣaṃ śrī-viṣṇum ||9||

entries.sanskrit: कृपणां बहु-भाषिणीं \[भा।पु। ३.१४.१६\] इति वक्ष्यति, तत्र एष माम् इति द्वाभ्यां कार्पण्यं, भर्तरीति चतुर्भिश् च बहु-भाषणं वर्ण्यते । दुनोति पीडयति । विक्रम्य शौर्यम् आविर्भाव्य । रम्भां कदलीम् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: by the two [verses] beginning ‘this one for me’
by the four [verses] beginning ‘in the husband’
entries.literal_english: The Bhāgavata will describe her as pitiable and talkative: her pitiableness is shown in these two verses and her excessive speech in the following four. “Dunoti” means pains; “vikramya” means manifesting power; rambhā is a plantain tree.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: kṛpaṇāṃ bahu-bhāṣiṇīṃ \[bhā|pu| 3.14.16\] iti vakṣyati, tatra eṣa mām iti dvābhyāṃ kārpaṇyaṃ, bhartarīti caturbhiś ca bahu-bhāṣaṇaṃ varṇyate | dunoti pīḍayati | vikramya śauryam āvirbhāvya | rambhāṃ kadalīm ||10||

entries.sanskrit: आयुङ्क्तां सर्वतो युनक्तु सम्यक् करोतु ॥११॥
entries.literal_english: May he join, or properly arrange, everything on every side.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: āyuṅktāṃ sarvato yunaktu samyak karotu ||11||

entries.sanskrit: भर्तरि प्राप्त-बहु-मानानां स्त्रीणां यशो लोकान् आविशते व्याप्नोति । प्रजया पुत्र-रूपेण । तज् जाया जाया भवति यद् अस्यां जायते पुनः इति श्रुतेः ॥१२॥
word_for_word: of women greatly honored by their husbands
in the form of a son
because what is born from her is born again
entries.literal_english: The fame of women who receive great honor from their husbands spreads through the worlds. Through offspring, the wife becomes fruitful; scripture says, “She is called wife because what is born from her is born again.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: bhartari prāpta-bahu-mānānāṃ strīṇāṃ yaśo lokān āviśate vyāpnoti | prajayā putra-rūpeṇa | taj jāyā jāyā bhavati yad asyāṃ jāyate punaḥ iti śruteḥ ||12||

entries.sanskrit: नोऽस्माकं पिता नोऽस्मान् पृथग् अपृच्छत् । अयं भावः---त्रयोदशानाम् अप्य् अस्माकं त्वयि भाव-साम्ये वैषम्याचरणं तवानुचितम् इति ॥१३॥
entries.literal_english: “He did not ask us separately, nor did our father ask us.” The point is that since all thirteen of us have equal affection for you, it was improper for you to act differently toward us.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: no’smākaṃ pitā no’smān pṛthag apṛcchat | ayaṃ bhāvaḥ---trayodaśānām apy asmākaṃ tvayi bhāva-sāmye vaiṣamyācaraṇaṃ tavānucitam iti ||13||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: मोघं न भवति हि । महीयसि त्वादृशे महत्तमे ॥१५॥
word_for_word: in a great person such as you
entries.literal_english: It is not fruitless, for it is done for one as great as you.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: moghaṃ na bhavati hi | mahīyasi tvādṛśe mahattame ||15||

entries.sanskrit: प्रवृद्धानङ्गेन कश्मलं मोहो यस्यास् ताम् ॥१६॥
entries.literal_english: Her delusion is the confusion produced by an enlarged passion.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: pravṛddhānaṅgena kaśmalaṃ moho yasyās tām ||16||

entries.sanskrit: सन्ध्या-काल-वञ्चनाय भार्या-प्रशंसा---एष इति पञ्चभिः । यतो यस्याः सकाशात् ॥१७॥
entries.literal_english: The praise of the wife for deceiving the twilight hour is given in these five verses. “From whom” means from whom it arose.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sandhyā-kāla-vañcanāya bhāryā-praśaṃsā---eṣa iti pañcabhiḥ | yato yasyāḥ sakāśāt ||17||

entries.sanskrit: सर्वाश्रमान् उपादायेति । तान् अप्य् अन्नादि-दानेन कृच्छ्रतस् तारयन् स्वयं तरतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: through gifts of food and the like
entries.literal_english: Taking all the āśramas together: by rescuing them with difficulty through gifts of food and the like, he himself crosses over and carries them across.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sarvāśramān upādāyeti | tān apy annādi-dānena kṛcchratas tārayan svayaṃ taratīty arthaḥ ||18||

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनो देहस्यार्धम् । कर्मसु द्वयोः सहाधिकारात् । यच्-छब्दानां तां त्वाम् इति तृतीय-श्लोकेन सम्बन्धः । स्व-धुरं दृष्टादृष्ट-कर्म-भारम् । विज्वरो निश्चिन्तः ॥१९॥
word_for_word: because husband and wife have joint authority in actions
the connection is with the third verse
the burden of visible and invisible duties
entries.literal_english: The half of his own body; husband and wife have joint authority in actions. The relative pronouns connect with “you” in the third verse. He is free from anxiety because he has placed upon himself the burden of visible and invisible duties.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: ātmano dehasyārdham | karmasu dvayoḥ sahādhikārāt | yac-chabdānāṃ tāṃ tvām iti tṛtīya-ślokena sambandhaḥ | sva-dhuraṃ dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-karma-bhāram | vijvaro niścintaḥ ||19||

entries.sanskrit: हेलाभिर् लीलाभिः । जयेमेति । स-भार्यस्येन्द्रियाणि प्रायेणेतस् ततो न सर्पन्तीति भावः ॥२०॥
word_for_word: of one accompanied by his wife
do not stray here and there
entries.literal_english: Through playful gestures. “May we conquer” means that, when accompanied by his wife, his senses generally do not stray here and there.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: helābhir līlābhiḥ | jayemeti | sa-bhāryasyendriyāṇi prāyeṇetas tato na sarpantīti bhāvaḥ ||20||

entries.sanskrit: ताम् अनेकोपकार-कर्त्रीं त्वां कार्त्स्न्येनानुकर्तुं प्रत्युपकारैस् त्वत्-सदृशा भवितुं न प्रभवो न समर्थाः । ये चान्ये गुण-गृध्नवो गुण-प्रियाः, तेऽपि न समर्थाः । सम्पूर्णेनाप्य् आयुषा । वा-शब्दाज् जन्मान्तरैर् अपि न प्रभव इत्य् उक्तम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: and those others who desire virtue
by the word ‘or,’ even through other births
entries.literal_english: Neither you nor those who love virtue can repay you fully for all the benefits you bestow or become your equal through reciprocal service—not even over a complete lifetime; the word “or” extends this to other births as well.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tām anekopakāra-kartrīṃ tvāṃ kārtsnyenānukartuṃ pratyupakārais tvat-sadṛśā bhavituṃ na prabhavo na samarthāḥ | ye cānye guṇa-gṛdhnavo guṇa-priyāḥ, te’pi na samarthāḥ | sampūrṇenāpy āyuṣā | vā-śabdāj janmāntarair api na prabhava ity uktam ||21||

entries.sanskrit: यद्य् अपि त्वद्-अनुकरणम् अशक्यम् । प्रजात्यै पुत्रोत्पत्त्यै । नातिरोचन्ति न निन्दन्ति । प्रतिपालय प्रतीक्षस्व ॥२२॥
entries.literal_english: Although imitating you is impossible, we ask you to beget offspring. They neither condemn nor greatly praise what has happened; wait and remain.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yady api tvad-anukaraṇam aśakyam | prajātyai putrotpattyai | nātirocanti na nindanti | pratipālaya pratīkṣasva ||22||

entries.sanskrit: स्व-निन्दाम् अगणयन्तीं भीषयन् श्री-रुद्रम् अनुवर्णयति---एषेति सप्तभिः । घोराणाम् एषा वेला । स्वयं च घोर-दर्शना ॥२३॥
word_for_word: and he himself is terrible to behold
entries.literal_english: To frighten Śiva while disregarding her own censure, she now describes him in seven verses. This is the terrible time, and he himself has a terrible appearance.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sva-nindām agaṇayantīṃ bhīṣayan śrī-rudram anuvarṇayati---eṣeti saptabhiḥ | ghorāṇām eṣā velā | svayaṃ ca ghora-darśanā ||23||

entries.sanskrit: भूत-पर्षद्भिर् भूत-गणैः ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: With hosts of spirits, with multitudes of beings.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: bhūta-parṣadbhir bhūta-gaṇaiḥ ||24||

entries.sanskrit: तर्हि तत्-संमुखत्व-मात्रं वर्जनीयम् इति चेत्, तत्राह---श्मशाने यश् चक्रानिलो वात-मण्डली, तस्मिन् या धूलिः, तया धूम्रो विकीर्णो विक्षिप्तो विद्योतो द्युतिमाञ् जटा-कलापो यस्य । भस्मनावगुण्ठः प्रावृतोऽमलो रुक्मवद् देहो यस्य, स देवस् त्रिभिः सोमार्काग्नि-नेत्रैः पश्यतीत्य् अस्योत्तर-श्लोक-त्रयेऽप्य् अनुषङ्गः । एकस्य जामातरः परस्परं भ्रातरो व्यवह्रियन्ते । अतो मम भ्राता असौ तव देवर इति लज्जार्थम् उक्तम् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: the stainless body shines like gold
with moon, sun and fire as eyes
entries.literal_english: If one says that merely facing him should be avoided, the answer is: in the cremation ground the wind raises a circle of dust, making his matted locks dusty and shining. His body is covered with ash yet gleams like gold, and he sees with three eyes—the moon, sun and fire. The sons-in-law of one person are mutually called brothers-in-law; therefore she says, for modesty, “He is my brother and your brother-in-law.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tarhi tat-saṃmukhatva-mātraṃ varjanīyam iti cet, tatrāha---śmaśāne yaś cakrānilo vāta-maṇḍalī, tasmin yā dhūliḥ, tayā dhūmro vikīrṇo vikṣipto vidyoto dyutimāñ jaṭā-kalāpo yasya | bhasmanāvaguṇṭhaḥ prāvṛto’malo rukmavad deho yasya, sa devas tribhiḥ somārkāgni-netraiḥ paśyatīty asyottara-śloka-traye’py anuṣaṅgaḥ | ekasya jāmātaraḥ parasparaṃ bhrātaro vyavahriyante | ato mama bhrātā asau tava devara iti lajjārtham uktam ||25||

entries.sanskrit: ननु तथापि महत्त्वेनादरणीयस्य स्व-जनस्य च तव स सर्वं क्षमेतैव तत्राह---यस्य स्व-जनादिर् नास्ति समत्वाद् ईश्वरस्य । ऐश्वर्यम् एवाह---येन चरणेनापविद्धां निर्माल्य-वद् दूरतस् त्यक्तां तेन भुक्त-भोगाम् अजां मायां तन्-मयीं विभूतिं महा-प्रसाद इत्य् आशास्महे । व्रतैस् तम् आराध्य ॥२६॥
word_for_word: of a great and respectable relative
he has no relatives or equals
discarded far away like a used garland
the enjoyed but delusive material nature
entries.literal_english: Even if one argues that a great and respectable relative should be honored and would forgive everything, the answer is that Śiva has no relatives or equals because he is the Lord. His sovereignty is shown by this: through vows we worship him and hope for the great blessing of his restoring the enjoyed but delusive material nature that he discarded as one throws away a used garland.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: nanu tathāpi mahattvenādaraṇīyasya sva-janasya ca tava sa sarvaṃ kṣametaiva tatrāha---yasya sva-janādir nāsti samatvād īśvarasya | aiśvaryam evāha---yena caraṇenāpaviddhāṃ nirmālya-vad dūratas tyaktāṃ tena bhukta-bhogām ajāṃ māyāṃ tan-mayīṃ vibhūtiṃ mahā-prasāda ity āśāsmahe | vratais tam ārādhya ||26||

entries.sanskrit: अनिषिद्ध-सुख-त्यागाद् असौ पिशाच इत्य् उपहासो न कार्य इत्य् आह द्वाभ्याम् । यस्यानवद्यं विषयासक्ति-शून्यम् आचरितम् । बिभित्सवो भेत्तुम् इच्छवः ॥२७॥
word_for_word: from giving up only prohibited pleasures
free from attachment to sense objects
entries.literal_english: The two verses say that one should not mock him as a ghost for giving up only prohibited pleasures. His conduct is faultless and free from attachment to sense objects; those who wish to break it are the offenders.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: aniṣiddha-sukha-tyāgād asau piśāca ity upahāso na kārya ity āha dvābhyām | yasyānavadyaṃ viṣayāsakti-śūnyam ācaritam | bibhitsavo bhettum icchavaḥ ||27||

entries.sanskrit: समीहितम् अभिप्रेतं लोक-शिक्षारूपम् । अविदुषोऽविद्वांसः । यद् वा, न विद्वान् अन्यो यस्माद् इति तस्य । सर्व-ज्ञस्येत्य् अर्थः । दुर्भगान् एवाह---यैर् इति । श्व-भोजनं शुनां भोज्यं शरीरम् । स्वात्मतयायम् एवात्मेति बुद्ध्या ॥२८॥
word_for_word: in the form of instruction of the world
the body is food for dogs
svātm atayā ayam evātmā iti buddhyā
with the notion ‘this alone is my self’
entries.literal_english: The intended purpose is instruction of the world. “Unlearned” means not knowing; alternatively, no one else is learned in comparison with him, for he is omniscient. She calls them unfortunate: their bodies are food for dogs, yet they think, “This alone is my self.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: samīhitam abhipretaṃ loka-śikṣārūpam | aviduṣo’vidvāṃsaḥ | yad vā, na vidvān anyo yasmād iti tasya | sarva-jñasyety arthaḥ | durbhagān evāha---yair iti | śva-bhojanaṃ śunāṃ bhojyaṃ śarīram | svātmatayāyam evātmeti buddhyā ||28||

entries.sanskrit: अहो अतर्क्यं तस्याचरणम् इत्य् आह---ब्रह्मादयो येन कृतान् सेतून् स्व-स्वाधिकारान् पालयन्ति । यः कारणं यस्य, येन कृतम् इदं विश्वम् । माया च यस्याज्ञा-करी । विभूम्नः परमेश्वरस्य विडम्बनम् अतर्क्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥
word_for_word: what an inconceivable conduct of his
by whom this universe was made
and māyā is obedient to him
entries.literal_english: She says, “What an inconceivable conduct!” Brahmā and the others preserve the boundaries of their respective offices; the Lord is the cause of the cause of this universe, and māyā obeys him. Thus the conduct of the all-pervading Supreme Lord is inconceivable.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: aho atarkyaṃ tasyācaraṇam ity āha---brahmādayo yena kṛtān setūn sva-svādhikārān pālayanti | yaḥ kāraṇaṃ yasya, yena kṛtam idaṃ viśvam | māyā ca yasyājñā-karī | vibhūmnaḥ parameśvarasya viḍambanam atarkyam ity arthaḥ ||29||

entries.sanskrit: भर्त्रा निरूपकेणैवं संविदिते ज्ञापितेऽपि सति । वृषलीव वेश्येव ॥३०॥
word_for_word: by the husband who should decide
entries.literal_english: Although her husband, who should have decided the matter, had explained it to her, she behaved like a low-born woman or a prostitute.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: bhartrā nirūpakeṇaivaṃ saṃvidite jñāpite’pi sati | vṛṣalīva veśyeva ||30||

entries.sanskrit: विकर्मणि निषिद्धे कर्मणि । दिष्टाय दैव-रूपायेश्वराय । उपविवेशेति मैथुनं लक्ष्यते ॥३१॥
word_for_word: to the Lord in the form of destiny
entries.literal_english: “Forbidden action” means an illicit act. “To destiny” means to the Lord in the form of destiny. “She sat down” indicates sexual union.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: vikarmaṇi niṣiddhe karmaṇi | diṣṭāya daiva-rūpāyeśvarāya | upaviveśeti maithunaṃ lakṣyate ||31||

entries.sanskrit: उपस्पृश्य स्नात्वा भर्ग-शब्द-वाच्यं विरजं ज्योतिर् ध्यायन् सनातनं ब्रह्म गायत्रीं प्रणवं वा जजाप ॥३२॥
entries.literal_english: After bathing, she touched water and meditated on the stainless, effulgent eternal Brahman denoted by bharga, reciting the Gāyatrī or praṇava.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: upaspṛśya snātvā bharga-śabda-vācyaṃ virajaṃ jyotir dhyāyan sanātanaṃ brahma gāyatrīṃ praṇavaṃ vā jajāpa ||32||

entries.sanskrit: कर्मावद्येन कर्म-दोषेण ॥३३॥
word_for_word: through the fault of the act
by the defect belonging to the action
entries.literal_english: Through the defect of the act, the fault belonging to the action.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: karmāvadyena karma-doṣeṇa ||33||

entries.sanskrit: नावधीन् मा हन्त्व् इत्य् अर्थः । वध-शङ्का-बीजम् आह---रुद्र इति । अंहसम् अंहोऽपराधम् अकरवं कृतवत्य् अस्मि ॥३४॥
word_for_word: na avadhīn mā hantv iti arthaḥ
‘may he not kill me’ is the meaning
the basis for fear of being killed
entries.literal_english: “May he not kill me” is the meaning. He gives the basis for fear of being killed: “Rudra.” “I have committed an offense” is the meaning of “I have done wrong.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: nāvadhīn mā hantv ity arthaḥ | vadha-śaṅkā-bījam āha---rudra iti | aṃhasam aṃho’parādham akaravaṃ kṛtavaty asmi ||34||

entries.sanskrit: रुद् दुःखं तद् द्रावयतीति रुद्रस् तस्मै । उग्रायानतिलङ्घ्याय मीढुषे स-कामेषु फल-सेचन-कर्त्रे । निष्कामेषु शिवाय । वस्तुतो न्यस्त-दण्डाय । दुष्टेषु धृत-दण्डाय संहारे मन्यवे ॥३५॥
word_for_word: to the fierce one who cannot be overstepped
to one who has laid down punishment
to one who holds the rod toward the wicked
entries.literal_english: Rudra is so called because he drives away sorrow. He is fierce and cannot be overstepped; as Mīḍhuṣ he showers fruits upon those who desire them; as Śiva he is gracious to the desireless; in truth he has laid down punishment, yet toward the wicked he holds the rod of punishment as the anger of destruction.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: rud duḥkhaṃ tad drāvayatīti rudras tasmai | ugrāyānatilaṅghyāya mīḍhuṣe sa-kāmeṣu phala-secana-kartre | niṣkāmeṣu śivāya | vastuto nyasta-daṇḍāya | duṣṭeṣu dhṛta-daṇḍāya saṃhāre manyave ||35||

entries.sanskrit: भामो भगिनी-भर्ता । उरुर् अनुग्रहो यस्य । व्याधस्य निर्दयस्यापि । सती-पतिर् इत्य् अनेन स्त्रीणां स्वभावं स्वयम् अपि वेत्तीति सूचयति ॥३६॥
entries.literal_english: Bhāma means a sister’s husband. He is exceedingly gracious, even toward a merciless hunter. By calling him the husband of Satī, she hints that he himself knows the disposition of women.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: bhāmo bhaginī-bhartā | urur anugraho yasya | vyādhasya nirdayasyāpi | satī-patir ity anena strīṇāṃ svabhāvaṃ svayam api vettīti sūcayati ||36||

entries.sanskrit: स्व-सर्गस्य स्व-सन्तानस्याशिषं शुभम् । लोक्यां लोक-द्वयार्हाम् । सन्ध्यायां यो नियमः स निवृत्तो यस्य ॥३७॥
word_for_word: of his own creation, his own offspring
entries.literal_english: The auspicious blessing of her own creation, her own offspring, should be for the world and worthy of both worlds. His twilight observance had ceased.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sva-sargasya sva-santānasyāśiṣaṃ śubham | lokyāṃ loka-dvayārhām | sandhyāyāṃ yo niyamaḥ sa nivṛtto yasya ||37||

entries.sanskrit: ते आत्मनश् चित्तस्याप्रायत्यादशुचित्वात् । मौहूर्तिकात् सन्ध्या-रूपात् । उत अपि मम निदेशस्याज्ञाया अति-चारेणाति-क्रमेण । देवानां रुद्रानुचराणाम् ॥३८॥
word_for_word: because they arose from fleeting twilight
they are attendants of the gods, of Rudra
entries.literal_english: They are impure because of the uncleanness of their minds, because they arose from the fleeting form of twilight, and because they transgressed my command. They are the attendants of the gods—of Rudra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: te ātmanaś cittasyāprāyatyādaśucitvāt | mauhūrtikāt sandhyā-rūpāt | uta api mama nideśasyājñāyā ati-cāreṇāti-krameṇa | devānāṃ rudrānucarāṇām ||38||

entries.sanskrit: एतैश् चतुर्भिर् हेतुभिर् जाठराधमौ पुत्रापसदौ । हे चण्डि कोपने ॥३९॥
word_for_word: the two degraded sons, inferior to true sons
entries.literal_english: For these four reasons they are the two degraded sons, inferior to true sons. “O Caṇḍi” means “O angry one.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: etaiś caturbhir hetubhir jāṭharādhamau putrāpasadau | he caṇḍi kopane ||39||

entries.sanskrit: हन्यमानानां सताम् ॥४०॥
word_for_word: of the virtuous who were being killed
entries.literal_english: Of the virtuous who were being killed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: hanyamānānāṃ satām ||40||

entries.sanskrit: शत-पर्व-धृक् वज्र-धर इन्द्रः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt
entries.literal_english: Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt with its hundred joints.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: śata-parva-dhṛk vajra-dhara indraḥ ||41||

entries.sanskrit: सुनाभेनोदारो बाहुर् यस्य । मह्यां मम कोपितेष्व् इत्य् उक्तत्वाच् छङ्कित-चित्ता सती प्रार्थयते, ब्राह्मणान् मा भूद् इति ॥४२॥
word_for_word: whose arm is generous with the Sudarśana wheel
may the brāhmaṇas not be harmed
entries.literal_english: He whose arm is generous with the Sudarśana wheel. Because she is alarmed by the statement “when they anger me,” Satī prays that the brāhmaṇas may not be harmed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sunābhenodāro bāhur yasya | mahyāṃ mama kopiteṣv ity uktatvāc chaṅkita-cittā satī prārthayate, brāhmaṇān mā bhūd iti ||42||

entries.sanskrit: नारका अपि तथा यां यां योनिम् असौ गतो भवति तत्र-स्थाश् च नानुगृह्णन्ति कृपां न कुर्वन्ति ॥४३॥
entries.literal_english: The beings in hell likewise do not show mercy or kindness to him in whatever womb he enters.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: nārakā api tathā yāṃ yāṃ yonim asau gato bhavati tatra-sthāś ca nānugṛhṇanti kṛpāṃ na kurvanti ||43||

entries.sanskrit: कृतो योऽपराधस् तेन शोकस् ततोऽनुतापस् तेन । प्रत्यवमर्शनाद् युक्तायुक्त-विचारात् । भगवति हरौ । भवे श्री-रुद्रे । एतैः पञ्चभिः कारणैः ॥४४॥
entries.literal_english: From the offense came sorrow, and from sorrow repentance; from reflection came discrimination between right and wrong. These five causes are related to Bhagavān Hari and to Bhava, Śrī Rudra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: kṛto yo’parādhas tena śokas tato’nutāpas tena | pratyavamarśanād yuktāyukta-vicārāt | bhagavati harau | bhave śrī-rudre | etaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ ||44||

entries.sanskrit: पुत्रस्य हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्राणां मध्ये एकः सतां मतो भविष्यति । तम् एव वर्णयति---गास्यन्तीति सार्धैः पञ्चभिः । समं सह स-दृक्षं वा ॥४५॥
entries.literal_english: Among the sons of Hiraṇyakaśipu he will be regarded as one of the virtuous. He now describes him in five and a half verses beginning with “they will sing.” “Samam” means together or equal.

transliteration: putrasya hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāṇāṃ madhye ekaḥ satāṃ mato bhaviṣyati | tam eva varṇayati---gāsyantīti sārdhaiḥ pañcabhiḥ | samaṃ saha sa-dṛkṣaṃ vā ||45||

entries.sanskrit: हीन-वर्णं हेम यथा योगैर् दाहादिभिर् उपायैः शोध्यते तथा यस्य शीलं स्वभावम् अनुवर्तितुम् अनुगन्तुं प्राप्तुं निर्वैरादिभिर् योगैर् आत्मानं भावयिष्यन्ति शोधयिष्यन्ति ।
word_for_word: just as by processes beginning with heating
by disciplines beginning with freedom from enmity
entries.literal_english: As impure gold is purified by processes such as heating, so they will cultivate and purify themselves by adopting his character through disciplines such as freedom from enmity.

transliteration: hīna-varṇaṃ hema yathā yogair dāhādibhir upāyaiḥ śodhyate tathā yasya śīlaṃ svabhāvam anuvartitum anugantuṃ prāptuṃ nirvairādibhir yogair ātmānaṃ bhāvayiṣyanti śodhayiṣyanti |

entries.sanskrit: विश्व-प्रसादे हेतुर् यद्-आत्मकम् । स्व-दृग् आत्म-साक्षी । यस्यानन्यया भगवान् एव सत्य इत्य् एवं-भूतया दृशा तोष्यते तोषं प्राप्स्यते ॥४७॥
word_for_word: the cause of the Lord’s favor
entries.literal_english: The cause of the Lord’s pleasure is that which is his very nature. “Self-seeing” means witnessing the self. The Lord is pleased by the person whose vision is exclusively fixed on him as the sole truth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: viśva-prasāde hetur yad-ātmakam | sva-dṛg ātma-sākṣī | yasyānanyayā bhagavān eva satya ity evaṃ-bhūtayā dṛśā toṣyate toṣaṃ prāpsyate ||47||

entries.sanskrit: तत्र हेतुः---स वा इति । महात्मा अविच्छिन्न-दृष्टिः महानुभावो महा-प्रभावः । महताम् अपि मध्ये महिष्ठोऽतिशयेन महान् । प्रवृद्धया भक्त्यानुभाविते शोधिते चित्ते वैकुण्ठं हरिं निवेश्य देहाद्य्-अभिमानं त्यक्ष्यति ॥४८॥
word_for_word: in a mind permeated and purified
he will abandon identification with the body and so forth
entries.literal_english: The cause is stated: he is such a one. He is a great soul, of uninterrupted vision and great power, the greatest among the great. With a mind purified and permeated by mature devotion, he will install Hari, Vaikuṇṭha, in his heart and abandon identification with body and other things.

transliteration: tatra hetuḥ---sa vā iti | mahātmā avicchinna-dṛṣṭiḥ mahānubhāvo mahā-prabhāvaḥ | mahatām api madhye mahiṣṭho’tiśayena mahān | pravṛddhayā bhaktyānubhāvite śodhite citte vaikuṇṭhaṃ hariṃ niveśya dehādy-abhimānaṃ tyakṣyati ||48||

entries.sanskrit: महा-भागवतत्वम् आह---अलम्पट इति । शील-धरः सु-स्वभावः । गुणानां धैर्यादीनाम् आकरो जन्म-भूमिः । परेषां समृद्ध्या हृष्टः । परेषु दुःखितेषु सत्सु । न भूतो जातः शत्रुर् यस्य । निदाघे भवं तापं चन्द्रो यथा हरत्य् एवं जगतः शोक-हर्ता भविष्यति ।।४९॥
word_for_word: he describes greatness as a mahā-bhāgavata
who has never had an enemy
he will become remover of the world’s sorrow
entries.literal_english: His greatness as a mahā-bhāgavata is described. He is free from greed and possesses good character; he is the source of virtues such as courage; he rejoices in others’ prosperity and grieves in their suffering; he has never had an enemy. As the moon removes the heat of summer, he will remove the world’s sorrow.

transliteration: mahā-bhāgavatatvam āha---alampaṭa iti | śīla-dharaḥ su-svabhāvaḥ | guṇānāṃ dhairyādīnām ākaro janma-bhūmiḥ | pareṣāṃ samṛddhyā hṛṣṭaḥ | pareṣu duḥkhiteṣu satsu | na bhūto jātaḥ śatrur yasya | nidāghe bhavaṃ tāpaṃ candro yathā haraty evaṃ jagataḥ śoka-hartā bhaviṣyati ||49||

entries.sanskrit: अपरिच्छिन्न-दृष्टित्वम् आह---अन्तर् इति । स्व-पुरुषाणाम् इच्छया पुनः पुनर् गृहीतानि रूपाणि येन । श्रीर् एव ललना सुन्दरी तस्या ललामं मण्डनम् । द्रष्टा द्रक्ष्यति ॥५०॥
word_for_word: at the wish of his own devotees
entries.literal_english: His uninterrupted vision is now described. He repeatedly assumes forms at the wish of his own devotees. Śrī is the beautiful woman, and her forehead ornament is the crest-jewel of adornment. He will see.

transliteration: aparicchinna-dṛṣṭitvam āha---antar iti | sva-puruṣāṇām icchayā punaḥ punar gṛhītāni rūpāṇi yena | śrīr eva lalanā sundarī tasyā lalāmaṃ maṇḍanam | draṣṭā drakṣyati ||50||

entries.sanskrit: महा-मनाः सोत्साह-चित्ता । हरिणा सह युद्धेन मरणे पुत्रयोः कीर्तिः सद्-गतिश् च भवेद् इति ॥५१॥
word_for_word: in the death of the two sons
fame and a good destination would result
entries.literal_english: He is great-minded and enthusiastic. If his two sons die in battle with Hari, they will gain fame and a good destination.
